title: From Externality to Civilizational Repair
subtitle: A Boundary-First learning pathway from familiar consequences to operational mechanics and repair
status: implementation-guidance draft; public copy and canonical promotion pending
claimCeiling: Public doctrine and operational orientation. The pathway explains and applies the current framework; it does not by itself establish formal or empirical claims.
thesis: Civilization acts through executable representations. Boundary First Labs develops the mechanics needed to keep those representations answerable to embodied consequence and capable of lawful revision.
sourceArtifacts: current project conversation: Abstraction Without Return through Public Mission

experienceContract.principle: One knowledge graph, several lawful projections.

modes.purpose: One memorable proposition and no more than three new canonical terms.
Persistent position, visible neighbors, resumable pathway state.
Open the deeper doctrine, evidence, examples, and source records without losing pathway state.
Manipulate a boundary, diagnose a defect, or choose a repair before continuing.

phases.label: Start with what people already experience
phases.purpose: Make displaced consequence visible before introducing theory.

phases.label: Name the structural pattern
phases.purpose: Show that the familiar failures are instances of abstraction without return.

phases.label: Make the pattern operable
phases.purpose: Connect accounting and software engineering to Boundary First mechanics.

phases.label: Show how systems revise or fail
phases.purpose: Introduce baseline formation, defect, promotion, and representational evolution.

phases.label: Scale the mechanics to civilization
phases.purpose: Unify accounting, software, agency, institutions, and evolution.

phases.label: Move from critique to repair
phases.purpose: Route diagnosed severances into concrete institutional and engineering responses.

card.title: There Is No More Outside
card.quote: Every externality is someone else’s internality.

expanded.summary: Modern people and institutions inhabit nested physical, social, legal, economic, computational, and ecological systems. A burden moved beyond one boundary does not disappear; it enters another interior.
expanded.mechanism: Externalization is a boundary crossing whose receiving system has been omitted from the acting system’s representation.
expanded.consequence: Waste enters a watershed, unpaid work enters a household, risk enters a public budget, and delay enters another team’s queue.
expanded.repair: Name the receiving system, preserve the transfer path, and distinguish burden resolution from burden relocation.

objectives: Distinguish disappearance from transfer
Recognize nested system boundaries
Identify the receiving interior
learning.prompt: Choose a familiar burden and trace where it goes when an organization calls it external.

microAssessment.success: The learner identifies a concrete receiving body, place, institution, or future period.

primary.implementation: hierarchy + partition with rounded nested rectangles

visualization.why: Nested rectangles make the no-floor claim literal: each apparent outside is visibly inside a larger enclosure. A transfer path shows that consequence crosses rather than vanishes.
visualization.dataShape: rooted containment hierarchy plus typed cross-boundary transfer edges
avoid: force-directed graph as the first view
geographic map unless the example is explicitly spatial
visualization.mobileFallback: Vertical nested cards with a stepwise burden trace.
visualization.reducedMotionFallback: Static before/after states with the receiving box highlighted.

accessibility.textTemplate: The burden leaves {source} and enters {receiver}; both are contained within {largerSystem}.

interaction.primaryAction: Drag a burden token across a boundary
interaction.onSuccess: Reveal the receiving interior and its repair capacity

transition.question: If the consequence remains inside the larger world, why was it called external?

card.title: Externality Is a Boundary Choice
card.quote: An externality is not outside the system. It is outside the system’s accounting.

expanded.summary: Accounting systems necessarily choose what to represent. The category of externality records a real consequence excluded by the chosen accounting boundary.
expanded.mechanism: Apparent gain is produced when benefits remain represented while burdens are transferred into unrepresented actors, lifecycle stages, or environments.
expanded.consequence: Local cost falls while household, public, ecological, maintenance, or future cost rises elsewhere.
expanded.repair: Expand the decision representation enough to include receiving actors, lifecycle burdens, uncertainty, and nonmonetary constraints without pretending every value is commensurable.

objectives: Treat externality as a declared boundary
Separate measurement difficulty from nonexistence
Trace benefit and burden together
learning.prompt: Toggle which costs are represented and watch the reported result change while the actual burden remains.

microAssessment.success: The learner can explain whose apparent efficiency depends on whose uncounted burden.

secondary.implementation: filter nodes by accounting inclusion state

visualization.why: A Sankey diagram shows that reducing a represented cost does not erase flow; it redirects burden into another node.
visualization.dataShape: directed weighted flows from activity to benefits and burdens, each tagged represented/unrepresented
visualization.mobileFallback: Ordered source → decision boundary → receiver flow list with quantities or qualitative severity.
visualization.reducedMotionFallback: Side-by-side inclusive and exclusive accounting states.

accessibility.textTemplate: {activity} produces {benefit} for {beneficiary} and transfers {burden} to {receiver}; the current accounting {includesOrExcludes} that burden.

interaction.primaryAction: Toggle actors and lifecycle stages inside the accounting boundary
interaction.onSuccess: Recalculate represented result and list still-unresolved nonmonetary constraints

transition.question: What kind of thing is making these boundary choices and acting through them?

card.title: Business Is Already Artificial Agency
card.quote: The corporation is the paper-speed ancestor of the artificial agent.

expanded.summary: A business preserves identity, senses conditions, records memory, selects actions, delegates work, transforms environments, and responds to feedback across time.
expanded.mechanism: Contracts, accounts, policies, governance, employees, software, capital, and infrastructure jointly form a persistent agency architecture.
expanded.consequence: The organization can act more coherently and persistently than any participant while responsibility disappears into distributed roles.
expanded.repair: Evaluate the full agency chain and bind delegated action to represented affected parties, interruptibility, accountability, and repair.

objectives: Recognize institutional agency without requiring consciousness
Map organizational components to agent functions
Locate responsibility gaps
learning.prompt: Map one ordinary business into sensing, memory, policy, action, feedback, and persistence.

microAssessment.success: The learner identifies both the acting organization and the humans or systems through which its agency is realized.

primary.implementation: fixed functional sectors around a central institutional identity

secondary.implementation: typed arrows for sense, decide, act, receive feedback

visualization.why: A constrained network reveals that the business is neither one person nor an inert container; it is a persistent loop composed of human, legal, financial, and computational parts.
visualization.dataShape: typed heterogeneous graph with functional roles and directed agency edges
avoid: anthropomorphic face or brain metaphor as the primary view
unconstrained force layout that scrambles functional roles
equating business and AI in every property
visualization.mobileFallback: Six-stage agent loop with expandable component lists.

accessibility.textTemplate: The organization senses through {sensors}, remembers through {memory}, decides through {policy}, acts through {actuators}, and persists through {persistenceMechanisms}.

interaction.primaryAction: Assign organizational parts to agent functions
interaction.onSuccess: Highlight any function with authority but no consequence return

transition.question: What changes when this paper-speed agent receives a bit-speed nervous system?

card.title: AI Accelerates Institutional Agency
card.quote: A business is already an artificial agent. AI gives it a faster nervous system.

expanded.summary: AI does not introduce constructed agency into an otherwise human-only world. It increases the speed, reach, memory, replication, and integration of existing institutional agents.
expanded.mechanism: Administrative sensing, classification, decision, communication, and execution move from meeting-and-paper cadence toward continuous computation.
expanded.consequence: Automation can remove not only wasteful delay but also review, appeal, contextual judgment, informal repair, and identifiable responsibility.
expanded.repair: Audit which larger agent the AI serves, which protective frictions it removes, who can interrupt it, and where responsibility and repair remain embodied.

objectives: Place AI inside a larger institutional agent
Distinguish wasteful from protective friction
Evaluate acceleration separately from objective quality
learning.prompt: Increase system speed and observe which review, appeal, or repair functions are bypassed.

microAssessment.success: The learner preserves at least one protective friction rather than treating all delay as waste.

primary.implementation: stable node positions with edge throughput and latency controls

secondary.implementation: optional animated tokens along decision edges

visualization.why: Keeping the same graph while changing rate makes the thesis legible: the category of agent remains, but the cadence and bypass risk change.
visualization.dataShape: agent graph plus latency, throughput, review gate, and interruptibility attributes
avoid: speed presented as intelligence or legitimacy
visualization.mobileFallback: Before/after agency loop with latency and removed-gate badges.

accessibility.textTemplate: At {rate}, the system completes {actions}; the following review gates are preserved: {preserved}; the following are bypassed: {bypassed}.

interaction.primaryAction: Adjust agency speed and toggle review gates
interaction.onSuccess: Show changed consequence radius and repair latency

transition.question: What common structural failure connects uncounted burdens, distributed agency, and accelerated decisions?

card.title: Abstraction Without Return
card.quote: The defining failure of the modern age is not abstraction itself. It is abstraction without return.

expanded.summary: Abstraction enables civilization, but it becomes dangerous when an agent, metric, category, decision, or claim no longer has a lawful path back to the reality it transforms.
expanded.mechanism: A capacity to act becomes separated from its required consequence, witness, maintenance, contestability, or repair path.
expanded.consequence: The excluded residue returns as exported defect borne by bodies, communities, infrastructure, ecosystems, maintainers, or future generations.
expanded.repair: Restore typed return paths between agency and consequence, representation and reality, authority and standing, construction and stewardship, and knowledge and provenance.

objectives: Recognize the common pattern across domains
Differentiate a root severance from a downstream symptom
Choose the correct root card for a case
learning.prompt: Select a consequence and identify which required relation was severed.

microAssessment.success: The learner can distinguish at least two plausible roots and justify the primary one.

primary.implementation: central root with ten severance branches and consequence leaves

visualization.why: A radial root structure makes the shared origin visible while preserving distinct branches. It supports card expansion without pretending the roots are identical.
visualization.dataShape: rooted doctrine tree with cross-links from each root to repair routes
avoid: ten equal cards with no shared structure
visualization.mobileFallback: Accordion root cards grouped by severance type.

accessibility.textTemplate: {root} separates {leftTerm} from {rightTerm}, producing {consequences}; its repair is {repair}.

transition.question: How can we integrate excluded consequences rather than merely criticize their exclusion?

steps.canonicalStatus: public doctrine and engineering bridge candidate

card.title: Accounting Meets Software Engineering
card.quote: Accounting declares what the system recognizes. Software engineering integrates what operation cannot afford to forget.

expanded.summary: Professional software engineering expands a normative happy-path representation into an operational system that includes actors, states, dependencies, exceptions, boundary conditions, observability, ownership, failure, recovery, and repair.
expanded.mechanism: Defects and edge cases reveal distinctions the original representation omitted but execution still requires.
expanded.consequence: When institutions retain narrow accounting while gaining software-speed execution, omitted consequences become faster and more systematic.
expanded.repair: Apply the same professional standard to civilizational accounting: represent ordinary and exceptional states, affected parties, lifecycle burdens, detection, ownership, rollback, and repair.

objectives: Connect externality accounting to edge-case integration
Distinguish happy-path completion from closure
Translate software practices into institutional design questions
learning.prompt: Start with a happy path and add the states reality forces the system to acknowledge.

microAssessment.success: The learner adds both a detection path and a responsible repair owner.

primary.implementation: layered directed graph with normal, exceptional, recovery, and escalation branches

secondary.implementation: solid normal flow, dashed failure flow, return repair flow

visualization.why: A layered DAG shows the exact professional move: a thin normative path becomes a richer executable state space with explicit failure and repair.
visualization.dataShape: directed state-transition graph with path kind, owner, witness, and closure status
avoid: treating all social values as software types
visualization.mobileFallback: Stepwise state machine with expandable exception and repair branches.

accessibility.textTemplate: The normal path moves from {start} to {success}. Failure {failure} is detected by {witness}, owned by {owner}, and repaired through {repairPath}.

interaction.primaryAction: Add an omitted actor, failure state, or lifecycle phase
interaction.onSuccess: Require witness, owner, and repair before the path can close

transition.question: What is the general mechanics behind boundary, omission, failure, and repair?

card.title: Boundary First
card.quote: Begin with the consequential boundary, what must remain true, where closure can fail, and who can repair it.

expanded.summary: Boundary First turns critique into a repeatable diagnostic and construction order.
expanded.mechanism: Pressure or need produces a distinction; the distinction is represented; transformations are admitted or refused; closure preserves an invariant or exposes a defect; repair revises the representation; stable structure may be promoted and reused.
expanded.consequence: Without explicit boundaries and closure criteria, systems confuse local completion with global success and hide repair in unrepresented people.
expanded.repair: Declare boundary, invariant, affected actors, admissible transformations, witnesses, failure modes, repair owners, and promotion conditions.

objectives: Use the four opening Boundary First questions
Trace a defect back to a representation
Separate repair from promotion
learning.prompt: Run one familiar case through boundary → invariant → defect → repair.

microAssessment.success: The learner states a protected invariant and a repair path rather than only describing harm.

primary.implementation: arc segments plus directed radial links

secondary.implementation: one stage activated at a time; user controlled

visualization.why: The radial cycle communicates recurrence and repair while direct stage selection supports operational learning.
visualization.dataShape: ordered cyclic states with success, defect, repair, and promotion branches
avoid: introducing the full formal vocabulary at once
visualization.mobileFallback: Vertical cycle with return arrows and a sticky current-stage card.
visualization.reducedMotionFallback: Static cycle with selection highlighting only.

accessibility.textTemplate: At {stage}, the system {action}. If {condition}, it proceeds to {successNext}; otherwise it exposes {defect} and returns through {repairNext}.

interaction.onSuccess: Unlock the full mechanics cycle and grammar overlay

transition.question: How do these cycles create new baselines rather than merely restore old ones?

card.title: Every Baseline Opens a Field of Variation
card.quote: Variation must cohere into a new baseline, restore the old one, or destroy the conditions that made it possible.

expanded.summary: Stable relations create a substrate upon which further variation can occur. New structures may remain transient, destabilize the substrate, or cohere strongly enough to become a new operative unit.
expanded.mechanism: Baseline → variation → interaction → restoration, collapse, or promotion into a successor baseline.
expanded.consequence: A higher-order system can consume the lower-order capacities upon which its own agency depends.
expanded.repair: Evaluate whether new agency preserves, repairs, and enlarges its enabling baselines rather than merely extracting from them.

objectives: Recognize substrate dependence across levels
Differentiate transient variation from promoted structure
Identify baseline consumption
learning.prompt: Choose a system and identify the lower-order capacities its higher-order agency requires.

microAssessment.success: The learner identifies an invariant of the substrate that the higher-order system must preserve.

primary.implementation: levels of stable organization along an ordered axis

secondary.implementation: collapse, restore, and promote branches at each level

visualization.why: The combined hierarchy and ordered progression shows that a new level becomes a substrate without ceasing to depend on the levels beneath it.
visualization.dataShape: ordered multilevel hierarchy with baseline dependencies and outcome branches
avoid: literal universal history claim with unsupported precision
single upward arrow implying guaranteed progress
collapsing particles, matter, cells, and institutions into identical mechanisms
visualization.mobileFallback: Stacked baseline ladder with expandable dependency and failure panels.
visualization.reducedMotionFallback: Static ladder and three outcome branches.

accessibility.textTemplate: {level} depends on {substrate}; variation can {restore}, {collapse}, or {promote} into {successor}.

interaction.primaryAction: Select a level and inspect its enabling substrate
interaction.onSuccess: Compare capacity creation with substrate consumption

transition.question: Can a system revise its governing representation before destructive selection does the work?

steps.canonicalStatus: central process candidate within Representational Mechanics

card.title: Representational Evolution
card.quote: A system survives by evolving its representations before reality breaks through them.

expanded.summary: Representations are necessarily incomplete and condition-bound. Systems fail when operating conditions change but their governing distinctions remain fixed.
expanded.mechanism: Representation → operation → contact with reality → defect → new distinction → revised representation → tested closure → promotion.
expanded.consequence: Exceptions multiply, manual repair accumulates, categories stop fitting, and institutions defend obsolete models against reality.
expanded.repair: Every consequential representation needs witnesses, challenge rights, revision triggers, protected invariants, test conditions, and a promotion path for repaired models.

objectives: Treat defects as evidence about representation
Distinguish behavioral adaptation from representation revision
Specify a lawful revision path
learning.prompt: Turn an accumulating exception into a candidate new distinction and test whether the revised model closes.

microAssessment.success: The learner names the omitted distinction, protected invariant, and evidence that would justify promotion.

primary.implementation: successive representation cycles positioned on expanding radius

secondary.implementation: branch rejected, repaired, and promoted revisions

visualization.why: A spiral preserves recurrence while showing that successful repair changes the baseline rather than returning to the identical starting point.
visualization.dataShape: ordered representation versions with defect evidence, tests, and promotion status
avoid: simple loop that implies no learning
visualization.mobileFallback: Version timeline with defect → revision → test → promotion cards.
visualization.reducedMotionFallback: Static stepped spiral or numbered timeline.

accessibility.textTemplate: Version {version} encountered {defect}; revision {revision} preserved {invariant}, passed {tests}, and received status {status}.

interaction.onSuccess: Compare old and new reachable states, defects, and preserved invariants

transition.question: What do we call this process when the represented and acting system is civilization itself?

card.title: Civilizational Mechanics
card.quote: Civilization is an executable representation that must learn to revise itself before it fails beneath its own model.

expanded.summary: Civilization acts through laws, accounting, institutions, organizations, infrastructure, software, and artificial agents. Together they represent people, resources, obligations, value, risk, and possible action.
expanded.mechanism: Accounting defines what enters collective consideration; institutions and software execute those representations; reality exposes omissions; representational evolution repairs them; civilizational closure preserves future possibility.
expanded.consequence: Locally aligned agents can accelerate globally defective representations until civilization consumes the baselines on which it depends.
expanded.repair: Develop Civilizational Mechanics as the scale-specific application of Representational Mechanics to collective accounting, agency, institutional evolution, and closure.

objectives: Unify accounting, software, agency, evolution, and civilization
Treat institutions as executable representations
Locate local/global closure failures
learning.prompt: Select a civilizational representation—law, metric, market rule, software system—and trace how it becomes action.

microAssessment.success: The learner traces representation → agent → action → affected system → consequence → repair.

primary.implementation: nested civilization layers: embodied life, households, organizations, institutions, infrastructures, biosphere

secondary.implementation: fixed anchor positions with force used only for collision and local adjustment

visualization.why: Nested layers show substrate dependence; cross-layer edges show that laws, accounts, software, and organizations execute across boundaries rather than staying inside one level.
visualization.dataShape: containment hierarchy plus typed execution, consequence, evidence, and repair edges
avoid: implying civilization can be engineered as one monolithic machine
visualization.mobileFallback: Layered vertical stack with selectable execution chains.
visualization.reducedMotionFallback: Static nested layers with one highlighted chain at a time.

accessibility.textTemplate: {representation} is executed by {agent} through {mechanism}, affecting {system}; consequence is witnessed by {witness} and repaired through {repair}.

interaction.primaryAction: Trace one executable representation end to end
interaction.onSuccess: Reveal missing standing, accounting, or repair links

transition.question: Which concrete repair path matches the failure you have diagnosed?

card.title: Route the Defect to Consequence Closure
card.quote: Critique becomes useful when the severed return path is made explicit and repairable.

expanded.summary: Different failures require different repairs. A missing cost is not repaired in the same way as missing standing, provenance, lifecycle ownership, or interruptibility.
expanded.mechanism: Diagnose the root severance, identify the receiving system and protected invariant, then select a repair route with an accountable owner, witness, test, and closure criterion.
expanded.consequence: Generic calls for responsibility often leave the agency architecture unchanged and return the burden to the same hidden human shock absorbers.
expanded.repair: Use a typed repair router rather than a universal moral slogan.

objectives: Match failures to repair mechanisms
Assign responsible capacity rather than blame alone
Define evidence of repair
learning.prompt: Choose the primary severance, then build a repair packet with owner, authority, resources, witness, and test.

microAssessment.success: The learner selects a route and supplies all required closure fields.

primary.implementation: roots on left, consequence classes in center, repair routes on right

secondary.implementation: stroke and pattern rather than color alone

visualization.why: The Sankey view makes many-to-many routing visible: one root can produce several consequences, and one repair route can address several roots without collapsing their distinctions.
visualization.dataShape: typed weighted tripartite graph: root → consequence → repair route
avoid: ranking harms on a single scalar
visualization.mobileFallback: Wizard: diagnose root → select consequence → construct repair packet.
visualization.reducedMotionFallback: Static highlighted path through the router.

accessibility.textTemplate: The diagnosed root {root} produces {consequence}. Recommended route {route} requires owner {owner}, witness {witness}, and closure test {test}.

transition.question: How does this pathway connect to the wider work of Boundary First Labs?

card.title: Keep the Future Open
card.quote: Boundary First Labs develops the representational mechanics civilization needs to recognize its consequences, repair its institutions, and evolve before it fails beneath its own models.

expanded.summary: The pathway now opens into the full Boundary First Labs atlas: theory, formal objects, engineering, agency, public consequence, evidence, and research programs.
expanded.mechanism: The learning sequence is a camera path through the same graph. Every concept introduced remains available as a node, doctrine card, repair route, or applied pathway.
expanded.consequence: Without the legend, the atlas appears as everything at once. With the pathway, the reader understands what kind of object each region contains and how critique connects to repair.
expanded.repair: Preserve the guided path, selected root, worked example, and repair route as emphasis layers when the complete atlas is revealed.

objectives: Locate the pathway within the wider atlas
Choose a next route by intent
Preserve the completed repair packet
learning.prompt: Choose where to continue: theory, engineering, science, public consequence, evidence, or a domain-specific repair path.

microAssessment.success: The learner can explain why the chosen next route follows from the diagnosed problem.

primary.layout: curated semantic coordinates with collision simulation
primary.implementation: manual cluster anchors; force only preserves spacing and drag behavior

secondary.implementation: zoom from completed pathway neighborhood to full atlas

visualization.why: The same nodes remain in place while context expands, preserving spatial memory and proving that the sequence and atlas are projections of one graph.
visualization.dataShape: typed content graph plus pathway emphasis and journey-state overlays
avoid: equal node size implying equal authority
removing the learner’s selected path on reveal
visualization.mobileFallback: Searchable clustered list with a focused neighborhood view and pathway emphasis.
visualization.reducedMotionFallback: Crossfade from pathway neighborhood to full atlas with stable node positions.

accessibility.textTemplate: The atlas contains {nodeCount} typed concepts. Your completed path emphasizes {path}; the recommended next regions are {regions}.

interaction.primaryAction: Open the atlas with pathway emphasis
interaction.onSuccess: Offer next routes without hidden profiling

transition.question: Which part of the work should become operative next?

rootCards.title: Agency and Consequence
rootCards.quote: Power becomes dangerous when it can act upon bodies and places without remaining attached to either.
rootCards.mechanism: Decision authority persists while exposure, dependence, maintenance, and repair are displaced.
rootCards.repairDoctrine: Bind agency to affected-party representation, consequence-bearing, stewardship, interruption, and enforceable repair.

rootCards.title: Representation and Reality
rootCards.quote: A representation becomes a defect when it forgets what reality still requires.
rootCards.mechanism: A metric, model, category, or interface becomes authoritative after its operating conditions and exclusions are forgotten.
rootCards.repairDoctrine: Declare what is preserved and forgotten; instrument omitted consequence; revise when closure fails.

rootCards.title: Authority and Standing
rootCards.quote: No one should be bound by a decision they have no meaningful way to contest.
rootCards.mechanism: People appear as classified objects but not as agents able to question, appeal, introduce evidence, or reopen a defective decision.
rootCards.repairDoctrine: No consequence without representation: preserve standing, explanation, contestability, and correction.

rootCards.title: Responsibility and Capacity
rootCards.quote: Responsibility becomes cruelty when it lands without authority, knowledge, resources, or repair capacity.
rootCards.mechanism: Those who decide are insulated while frontline workers, households, operators, or local institutions absorb repair obligations.
rootCards.repairDoctrine: Align authority, knowledge, resources, responsibility, consequence, and repair capacity.

rootCards.title: Construction and Stewardship
rootCards.quote: Nothing is truly built until maintenance, repair, replacement, and retirement are accounted for.
rootCards.mechanism: Initial production is rewarded while ongoing operation and eventual repair are assigned elsewhere or nowhere.
rootCards.repairDoctrine: No product without stewardship and closure; represent the full lifecycle before construction is approved.

rootCards.title: Value and Durable Capacity
rootCards.quote: Value is false when gain is counted here and damage is carried elsewhere.
rootCards.mechanism: Benefits are captured inside the valuation boundary while depleted labor, infrastructure, ecology, trust, and future options remain outside it.
rootCards.repairDoctrine: Count displaced burden, resilience, lifecycle cost, repair, and future option space wherever value is claimed.

rootCards.title: Local Success and Systemic Closure
rootCards.quote: A system has not succeeded when its parts win by making the whole less viable.
rootCards.mechanism: Subsystems optimize within narrow boundaries and transfer defect into the systems that sustain them.
rootCards.repairDoctrine: Admit local action only when the necessary invariants of larger containing systems remain preserved.

rootCards.title: Legibility and Reciprocity
rootCards.quote: Power should not see downward more clearly than it can be seen upward.
rootCards.mechanism: People become governable data objects while decision procedures, incentives, and responsible actors remain opaque.
rootCards.repairDoctrine: Expose what accountability and repair require; protect what dignity and independent agency require.

rootCards.title: Language and Operational Meaning
rootCards.quote: A word becomes an instrument of capture when its public meaning and operative meaning diverge.
rootCards.mechanism: Institutions inherit legitimacy from ordinary language while executing narrower or incompatible definitions.
rootCards.repairDoctrine: Define consequential terms by boundary, test, exclusion, actor, and translation rule. No undeclared we.

rootCards.title: Knowledge and Provenance
rootCards.quote: Knowledge without a return path to witness becomes rhetoric with inherited authority.
rootCards.mechanism: Summaries, generated statements, and institutional conclusions circulate after their evidence and conditions disappear.
rootCards.repairDoctrine: Preserve the path from claim to source, method, witness, criticism, correction, and supersession.

repairRoutes.title: Consequence Accounting
useWhen: burdens are excluded from the decision boundary
future or nonmonetary effects are invisible
operations: preserve qualitative constraints where monetization is invalid
recalculate the decision under inclusive scenarios
repairRoutes.closureTest: No material predictable burden remains unnamed, ownerless, or misdescribed as resolved when it has only been transferred.

repairRoutes.title: Agency Governance
useWhen: constructed agents act through distributed people and software
repairRoutes.closureTest: Every consequential action has an accountable authority, visible affected parties, an interruption path, and a funded repair owner.

repairRoutes.title: Standing and Contestability
useWhen: people are classified or governed without recourse
the affected party cannot introduce evidence
repairRoutes.closureTest: An affected person can understand, challenge, correct, and obtain remedy for a defective consequential decision.

repairRoutes.title: Responsibility–Capacity Alignment
useWhen: an owner lacks authority or resources
operations: move authority toward responsibility or responsibility toward authority
repairRoutes.closureTest: No party remains accountable for an outcome they lack the authority, knowledge, resources, or lawful path to repair.

repairRoutes.title: Lifecycle Stewardship
useWhen: construction is funded but maintenance is not
operations: define decommissioning and data or material disposition
repairRoutes.closureTest: The created system has viable operation, maintenance, repair, replacement, and retirement paths before launch.

repairRoutes.title: Provenance and Witness
repairRoutes.closureTest: Every consequential claim retains a reconstructible path to evidence, method, criticism, and correction.

repairRoutes.title: Local–Global Closure
useWhen: one subsystem exports defect to another
operations: limit actions that consume shared baselines
repairRoutes.closureTest: Local success remains admissible after its consequences are transported through every materially affected containing system.

repairRoutes.title: Representational Revision
repairRoutes.closureTest: The revised representation handles the exposed defect, preserves required invariants, and contains a lawful path for future revision.

viewRegistry.principle: A view is a projection of the content graph plus pathway overlays; it is not a separate ontology.

views.d3Use: camera, transitions, and small stage-specific diagrams

views.primaryQuestion: What surrounds and conditions this object?
views.d3Use: cluster, linkRadial, arc, fixed semantic rings

views.primaryQuestion: What contains, grounds, or descends from what?
Where does benefit, burden, authority, or repair travel?
What states and transitions are admissible?
views.d3Use: d3-shape links and arcs, d3-dag for acyclic portions

views.primaryQuestion: How does the complete body connect?
views.d3Use: curated coordinates, force collision, zoom, filters
only small local diagrams; prose and evidence remain primary

selectionRules: Use hierarchy only when containment or descent is the claim.
Use Sankey only when flow or transfer is the claim; do not imply numerical precision when only qualitative weight is known.
Use force layouts for networks, not hierarchy; preserve curated anchors for canonical architecture.
Use radial layouts for one focus with three to seven primary neighbors or a genuinely cyclic mechanism.
Use state diagrams when admissibility and transition matter more than conceptual proximity.
Use cards and prose when the relationship is primarily doctrinal rather than geometric.
Every visualization has a text alternative, stable keyboard order, mobile fallback, and reduced-motion form.
